display.title: Episode 323: King David's Grave (Parshas Shemini, Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah-time show without music: Ahavas Yisroel and Rabbi Akiva's students, the signs of a kosher animal from Parshas Shemini, and a miracle at the cave of King David's grave.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Shemini, during Sefiras HaOmer, so the show opens without music. Uncle Yossi explains that Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague in these days because they did not show each other respect, and that we answer with Ahavas Yisroel and achdus. Then, following the Alter Rebbe's teaching to 'live with the times', he opens the Chumash to Parshas Shemini and teaches the two signs of a kosher animal, split hooves and chewing the cud, with examples of the pig, the camel and the rabbit, and explains that Hashem gave these laws out of love, like a father caring for his child's health. A yeshiva student in Studio 604 leads the Shema. Story time tells how a visiting king's precious sword fell into the sealed cave of King David's grave in Yerushalayim. Two servants sent down never returned, until the local rabbi, after the community recited the whole Tehillim, went down and came back with the sword, telling of a great light. The king rewarded the Jews with freedom to keep the Torah. The show ends with the Sefirah lesson, mission cards and Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Love and respect every Jew during Sefirah; and keep kosher, because Hashem gave us these laws out of love.
